teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner pronounces French loanword 'chef' as /tʃɛf/.
💡 Solution: Classify CH by origin: Chef = French (/ʃ/), School = Greek (/k/), Church = Germanic (/tʃ/).

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Etymological Strata (Greek, French, Latin, Germanic)
1. Definition: English vocabulary consists of four historical strata, each retaining its original pronunciation rules.

2. Rule: 1. Greek: CH = /k/ (school, chrome), PH = /f/ (phone), PS/PN silent initial (psychology, pneumonia). 2. French: CH = /ʃ/ (chef, machine), -QUE = /k/ (unique), -ETTE stressed (cassette). 3. Latin: Soft C/G, palatal TI/CI/SI (/ʃ, ʒ/), -TION. 4. Germanic: CH = /tʃ/ (church), hard G (get), silent GH (night), KN/WR/MB silent.
3. Why? English imported loanwords wholesale without converting their original spelling systems.
4. How to recognize? Identify word origin markers in formal vs informal vocabulary.
5. Common examples: Greek: school /skuːl/, chef /ʃɛf/ (French), church /tʃɜːrtʃ/ (Germanic), unique /juːˈniːk/ (French), nation /ˈneɪʃən/ (Latin)
6. Counter-examples: Hybrid words combining roots from different strata.
7. Exceptions: Assimilation of older loanwords into Germanic speech patterns.
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing French 'chef' as Germanic /tʃɛf/ or Greek 'chrome' as /ʃroʊm/.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Greek CH=/k/! French CH=/ʃ/! Germanic CH=/tʃ/!
10. Key vocabulary: etymology, lexical strata, Greek borrowing, French borrowing, Germanic core
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🟣 C1
13. Associated Visual: 🏛️ 4 Pillars representing Germanic, Latin, French, and Greek roots.
14. Key Takeaway: Word origin determines pronunciation! CH = /tʃ/ (Germanic), /k/ (Greek), /ʃ/ (French)!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: How is CH pronounced in Greek origin words like 'school' and 'chrome'? (/k/ sound)
CCQ 2: How is CH pronounced in French origin words like 'chef' and 'machine'? (/ʃ/ sh sound)
CCQ 3: How is CH pronounced in native Germanic words like 'church' and 'child'? (/tʃ/ ch sound)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.
